title: Simultaneous ringed slices and their invertible adjunction mates
statement: For small finitely complete E with subcanonical topology K, a fully faithful finite-limit-preserving F:E→Sh(J), a specified Hom nerve equivalence N, and a ringed equivalence g with invertible structural map inducing N, fix exact whole module data [def-sp-binary-presentation-module-data], four subterminal images F(Zi), and specified element-site and actual localized-site slice equivalences with their Hom formula. There exist localized ringed equivalences to the fixed rings A.over Zi, with module and ordinary derived equivalences, commuting with restriction and further restriction with the exact identity/composition HEq equations. For every choice of left or right adjoints, the actual mates of the comparison squares are invertible. This is the ringed and adjunction part of the binary presentation; no small-category construction or binary-cover hypothesis occurs.

source.place: Tags 00Y1, 04GZ and 03EH; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CR and 04IE. Auxiliary extraction of the corresponding steps of lem-sp-binary-cover-site-presentation.

proof.text: For each Zi use [lem-sp-nerve-ringed-localization] to get the localized ringed morphism, its inverse-image equality, invertible structural map, module comparison data and restriction square.
Apply [lem-sp-nerve-module-restriction-coherence] to choose simultaneous restriction/further squares and their three coherence equations.

For an invertible square between equivalences, use the adjunction Hom equivalences on each side. Postcomposition with the right mate on maps from E(X) is the composite of the first equivalence Hom bijection, first adjunction inverse Hom bijection, second equivalence Hom bijection, conjugation by the square, and second adjunction Hom bijection. The mate counit equation proves this formula. Essential surjectivity extends bijectivity to all objects, and Yoneda proves the mate invertible. Dually, precomposition with the left mate is a composite of Hom bijections by its unit equation; coyoneda proves it invertible. Package these mates with the comparisons, leaving their component maps and HEq equations unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_binaryPresentationSlices
    {C E : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory E] [HasFiniteLimits E]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology E} [K.Subcanonical]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (ring : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : E ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)) [F.Full] [F.Faithful] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (Z : Fin 4 → E) (hsub : ∀ i : Fin 4, IsSubterminal (F.obj (Z i)))
    (N : Sheaf J (Type u) ≌ Sheaf K (Type u))
    (hN : N.functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf K (Type u) ≅ sheafSubcategoryNerve F)
    (ringed : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings ring) (localCoefficientRings R))
    (hi : ringed.inverse = N.functor) (_hd : ringed.direct = N.inverse)
    (hr : IsIso ringed.ringMap) (whole : BinaryPresentationModules ringed)
    (sourceSlice : ∀ i : Fin 4,
      RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData (localCoefficientRings R) (F.obj (Z i)))
    (slice : ∀ i : Fin 4, Over (F.obj (Z i)) ≌ Sheaf (K.over (Z i)) (Type u))
    (hSlice : ∀ i : Fin 4,
      (slice i).functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (K.over (Z i)) (Type u) ≅
        yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft (Over (Z i))ᵒᵖ
          (Over (F.obj (Z i)))ᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj (Over.post F).op) :
    Nonempty (BinaryPresentationSlices R ring F Z ringed whole sourceSlice slice)
